risks.risk: The laptop may have been reflashed or has a non-genuine OS, affecting warranty or performance.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the BIOS/UEFI screen showing the model and serial number, or a full system information tool output (like HWiNFO) showing hardware details.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially non-genuine or modified, which may reduce value.

risks.risk: The display resolution and color gamut (WQXGA, 100% sRGB) are not verifiable from photos and may be inaccurate.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the display settings showing resolution (e.g., 3840x2400) and color profile, or a calibration report.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown display quality, which may reduce value for buyers seeking high-end visuals.

risks.risk: The GPU may be underclocked or have performance issues not visible in Task Manager.
risks.proof: A benchmark screenshot (e.g., 3DMark, FurMark) showing GPU performance and temperatures.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially underperforming, which may reduce value.

risks.risk: The storage may be a lower-tier SSD or have reduced lifespan.
risks.proof: A screenshot of CrystalDiskInfo or similar tool showing SSD health, model, and wear level.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown storage condition, which may reduce value.

proof_requests: Screenshot of BIOS/UEFI showing model and serial number.
Screenshot of display settings showing resolution and color profile.
CrystalDiskInfo screenshot showing SSD health and model.
response.reason: The laptop is identifiable as an Alienware 16 Aurora ACH250 with 16GB RAM and Intel Core i7-240H. The 5.2GHz max turbo claim is contradicted by the 2.50GHz base clock shown. Display specs are unverifiable. Risks exist but are common in used laptops; the item can be priced at its worst case (e.g., display not WQXGA, GPU not performing at max) and adjusted upward with proof.
